How is Gears of War so popular? Well...

Rule of cool, chainsaw Lancers, active reload system granting increased bullet damage for those who timed their reloads well, bullet-sponge-based gameplay that forced players to find quicker ways to dispatch foes and more depth than just "cover based gameplay". If you truly think that's its singular trump card when it comes to game design (like Yahtzee Croshaw liked to make fun of), then you're really not playing the game to its strengths - and as a result your experience will suffer, because you're sitting behind a wall and not utilising all the tools that you are given (including weapons that have specific mechanics and unique abilities like the Lancer's instakill chainsaw ability on non-Lancer wielding enemies) to their fullest potential.

Essentially the whole metagame of Gears of War was designed very purposefully (from the sniper rifles to the shotguns) to be a slow, methodical game that rewarded aggressive play and finely-tuned reflexes. Put this in an industrial scifi setting with charismatic characters (Cole Train, baby! WHOOO!) and you've got a game with a lot of character, depth (not complexity, mind), and a gloriously slick D-Pad weapon swap system that allows players to carry four unique weapons so that they can constantly swap-up the way they play to counter new threats. Halo has nothing on Gears of War when it comes to the weapon meta-game as a result - compare swapping between two weapons (and a hot button tied to throwing grenades) to four unique weapons and the ability to either lob grenades underhand or chuck 'em as far as you can. Compare GoW to UT4, however, and being able to carry more weapons doesn't necessarily make a game better than another one - UT4 is based on a more classic arena shooter setup where guns are treated as a resource: collecting them all controls the battlefield in your favour.

If you've seen any competitive matches of Gears of War players at their peak, you'd see just how brutally quick-paced and not at all stagnant/stationary behind walls it is as the players utilise all of their equipment, abilities, dodge rolls and clambers to effectively dance around their opponents whilst slaughtering them.

It's beautiful.
